$comment: Part I Section C — the procurement procedure and project. Hand-authored (not compiler-generated). Field set grounded in the Schematron: cbc:ProcedureCode is MANDATORY (BR-SC-10, fatal); identifiers carry a mandatory @schemeAgencyID (BR-OTH-02, fatal); the lot list is what selection criteria reference (BR-LOT-41). cac:ProcurementProject name/description and cac:ProcurementProjectLot have no presence rule and are optional here.
title: ESPD Part I Section C — Procurement Procedure and Project

procedure.description: The procurement procedure itself (PI03). Maps to document-header elements, not to a cac: aggregate.

procedureType.description: Type of procedure as a procurement-procedure-type code (e.g. 'Open'). Maps to cbc:ProcedureCode, which BR-SC-10 makes mandatory. NOTE: no .gc for this list is shipped in ESPD-EDM/codelists and the CVA does not validate cbc:ProcedureCode, so no enum can be derived — unlike Section A's publication type. The value is therefore unconstrained here.
procedureType.$comment.noEnum: No DocrefcontentType-style enum: the procurement-procedure-type .gc is not shipped. See codelist-attributes.json 'procurement-procedure-type' $note.

fileReference.description: The buyer's own reference number for this procedure. Maps to cbc:ContractFolderID. BR-OTH-02 (fatal) requires a non-empty @schemeAgencyID on the element; it is supplied as a constant 'OP' at export (the file reference is the buyer's own internal reference, with no scheme to derive an agency from), so it is not stored here.

value.description: The file reference number (e.g. 'PP.20170419.1024-9'). Maps to the text of cbc:ContractFolderID.

project.description: The procurement project (EA I70 'info-pp'). Maps to cac:ProcurementProject. No Schematron rule requires either child; the BASE sample carries only a Description.

name.description: Short title of the procurement. Maps to cac:ProcurementProject/cbc:Name.

description.description: Description of the procurement. Maps to cac:ProcurementProject/cbc:Description.

lots.description: The lot identifiers this procedure is divided into (LOT-0000, LOT-0001, …). The UI collects a 'Number of lots' count and generates this array; it is the canonical stored form. Each id maps to one cac:ProcurementProjectLot/cbc:ID carrying the criterion identifier scheme. Lots are a DOCUMENT-level mechanism (one Request per procedure); selection criteria reference these ids via cac:ProcurementProjectLotReference, which BR-LOT-41 makes mandatory for every selection criterion. OPTIONAL overall (a procedure need not be divided into lots), but non-empty WHEN PRESENT — a count of 0/blank stores no `lots` key at all rather than an empty array.
